Commentary.Commentary: What is your view about 195 as the target? 40 overs for Pakistan to make it 2-0? Or can Zimbabwe give it a good fight by taking 5-6 wickets? The run chase begins at 1330 local (1130 GMT).

Sarfraz Ahmed was in a bad mood throughout the innings. 'AREY JALDI KARO, JALDI KARO!' was his gibbering throughout. Don't understand why though. Must not have slept peacefully like my office colleagues, who struggled to reach on time to office today owing to the hangover of the FIFA World Cup. But in spite of the cold conditions, the bowlers did really well. Usman Khan bowled the best of them, going for around 1 an over in Powerplay 1 and then coming back well at the death too - returning with figures of 4/36. As usual, Hasan Ali got wickets too with a triple against his name. Shadab Khan had trouble gripping the ball and struggled.

Two batsmen scored fifties - Hamilton Masakadza and Peter Moor - in different areas of the game. The skipper was responsible for an uplift in the run rate while the latter did well to hang around almost till the end. Nothing much in the middle, except for a couple of starts from Musakanda and Murray.

Another sad outing for the home side. They showed a lot of promise in the first half of the innings, managing to reach 100 and losing just 3 wickets. But once captain Masakadza fell, so did the promise.

OUT! Another Pakistan fielder finds the stumps. Zimbabwe do not play out their 50 overs. On middle, Muzarabani pushes it towards mid on. There is a yes-yes no-no between the batsmen - just like you see between a number 10 and a number 11. Eventually, Chatara is sold a dummy down the river but he tries to get back. But Fakhar Zaman finds the stumps with an accurate throw. Hasan Ali is lucky - because had Zaman missed, the throw was heading right to Hasan's face. ZIMBABWE MANAGE 194!
A slower ball outside off, a wild slog from Muzarabani results in nothing.
Excellent yorker on middle, well dug out.
The batsman has driven it through mid on.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
Driven through the covers by the batsman.
A fine yorker, Chatara just gets his bat down in time to dig it out towards square leg. A single taken.
Full and straight, pushed away defensively.
Blessing Muzarabani is the last man in.

OUT! That is the end of Moor. It is a short ball, yes, but on the slower side. Peter pulls hard but has got more height than distance. Only finds Shoaib Malik at the mid-wicket fence. End of a decent knock from Moor. Who knows what might have happened had the partnership with Masakadza lasted longer - people in this cabin would have had to purchase hats first, so that they can eat them for predicting that Zimbabwe will get bowled out under 200.
Excellent yorker, well dug out.
The batsman failed to make contact and was hit low on the pads. Leg bye given by the umpire.
HALF CENTURY FOR MOOR! Just his third in this format. He has managed to fight hard and keep Zimbabwe in the hunt for a respectable total. On middle and leg, flicked through the leg side for a single.
Tendai Chatara comes in. Zimbabwe have got 16 balls left... can they play out those? Try and get to 200-210?

OUT! Masakadza is well short! Boy, I do need to check my eyes, my spectacles and even my cornea. That did not look out at all. But replays show otherwise. On middle and leg, Masakadza pushed it to the leg side and set off for a single. There was a bit of a stutter from him, looking at his partner and then he continued running. Meanwhile, Hasan Ali showed how good a fielder he is too as he charged to the ball, picked it up in one go and aimed at the stumps - hitting the bull's eye. Replays also show that while reaching the other end, Wellington slowed down a touch - probably with the fear of getting hurt - that cost him big time.
A direct hit. Referred upstairs. To the naked eye, Wellington seems comfortably in...
Short and outside off, cut through point for a single.
Hasan Ali is back on. 7-1-30-2 so far. Would be interesting to see how he celebrates if he gets a wicket.
Outside off, played straight to point.

Great running, fielding. Amir bowls a peach again, reversing the ball from a fuller length, around middle, WM flicks it through square leg. The fielder takes it lightly and the batsmen pounce on the opportunity to take the second. The throw coming in at the bowler's end is pretty weak and Moor makes it in comfortably.
Terrific ball. Comes in a bit wider of the crease and bowls it extremely full, reversing it. Wellington initially looks to drive but just about manages to counter the swing with a defensive flick.
Outside off, coming in, not giving much room, pushed towards point.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
Around off, angling in, defended watchfully.

On middle and leg, Masakadza helps it behind square on the leg side and gets a couple of runs. A rare expensive over from Usman - going for 12 - he finishes with his second best figures in ODIs - 10-1-36-4.
Down the leg side, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
Around off, pushed towards cover.
SIX! Effortless shot! Backs away to the leg side, Usman follows him and Moor just lofts it straight back. Does not have enough strength but plenty of timing on it. Just about clears the sightscreen.
Outside off, flayed through the covers for a couple.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover.
Outside off, steered to third man for a run.
Around off, defended watchfully from his crease.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Outside off, played through point for a single.
FOUR! Nicely done. A full toss, on middle, Masakadza whips it behind square leg for a boundary.
Short and outside off, Masakadza slashes hard but gets a bottom edge which goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Mohammad Amir is back on. 6-0-21-0 so far.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Right through him. Usman lands it on a length, around off and Moor looks to defend but the ball sneaks past the inside edge.

ALMOST THE HAT-TRICK! The wood saves Wellington there. On middle and leg, Masakadza looks to tuck it fine but misses and is hit on the pads. Seems a prime candidate for LBW but then everyone realizes an inside edge involved. A run taken to fine leg.
Who's in next to face the music of the hat-trick? Wellington Masakadza it is.

OUT! Dead plumb LBW now. Pakistan hastening Zimbabwe's innings to conclusion here. Usman Khan is on a hat-trick. Full and straight, Roche shuffles across a touch to play it through the leg side but misses. Cannot do that to such balls. Ian Gould barely takes a second to raise the finger.
Liam Roche is the new man in.

OUT! The middle stump takes a beating this time. A pinpoint yorker, right at the base of the stumps, Tiripano backs away and looks to hit it through the off side but misses. Bang. Sound of timber getting uprooted.
Down the leg side, Tiripano looks to tuck it away but misses. The ball goes off his pads to the leg side and the batsmen take a leg bye.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. A rare bad day for Shadab - 10-0-47-0 today.
The batsman plays the square cut.

MISFIELD, FOUR! The fielders are doing well to keep Sarfraz boiling like a tea pot. Full and outside off, Tiripano blasts it through the covers. Imam-ul-Haq comes running across to his left, should have made a regulation stop, but tumbles and parries the ball over!
Drives this past the diving bowler towards long off for a run.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a single.
Short and outside off, cut through point for a couple.
The batsman gets an inside edge and the ball hits him on the pads.
TOP EDGE, SAFE! A short ball, on middle, Tiripano looks to pull but the bounce gets big on him and goes off the top edge. Fine leg comes running in but cannot get to the ball. A single taken.
Pushes this towards cover for a run.
Excellent yorker, on middle, well dug out.
On middle and leg, defended watchfully.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Short again, this time he finds the gap through point for a couple.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
It's been driven superbly through the covers.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, Moor drives it straight back. Shadab dives to his left but misses. A single taken.
Full on middle, pushed to the bowler.
On middle and leg, tucked through the leg side for a single.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
WIDE. Bangs it short, way down the leg side, Moor looks to flick but misses.
Full and around off, driven straight back past the bowler for a run.
Around off, watchfully defended.
A short ball outside off, guided towards third man for a single.
Usman Khan is back into the attack. 6-1-17-2 so far.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
A touch short, punched wide of cover for a run.
Outside off, left alone.
The googly, on middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, Moor gets down to slog but misses.
Full and around off, pushed down to long on for a single.
FOUR! Cheeky! A short ball outside off, Moor arches back, waits for the ball to come to him and upper cuts it over the keeper to the third man fence!
WIDE. Some chin music for the batsman, he lets that bouncer through to the wicket-keeper. Wide signalled by the umpire.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
The batsman plays it with an angled bat and guides it to third man. One run added to the total.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Outside off, coming in again, left alone once more.
We are into the bowlers now. Donald Tiripano is the first of them, at number 7.

OUT! The off stump has taken a beating. Superb bowling. But has Hasan Ali hurt himself? He can get what my colleague is getting for himself right now -  a neck message. He was trying to celebrate in his usual manner, trying to swing his hands ferociously, only to find some pain in the left side of his neck. Coming to the ball, he lands it on a length outside off, Murray looks to defend but is comprehensively beaten for pace. The ball darts in, goes past the bat and KABOOM.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.
Tossed up outside off, watchfully defended.
The batsman drives this through the covers. They pick up a single.
Outside off, a push and a miss.
Full and outside off, driven past the bowler towards long off for a single.
On middle and off, punched back to the bowler.
On middle and leg, flicked straight to short mid-wicket. A MAIDEN for Hasan.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Beaten. On a length outside off, extra bounce, Murray flashes hard but misses.

DRINKS BREAK. Zimbabwe have done well. They have managed to lose only 4 wickets in 70 percent of their innings so far. There is nothing much on the pitch though and considering that Pakistan bowlers are struggling with the cold, the batsmen should try and start thinking about accelerating. Can they try and get to 250 and make it an interesting contest?
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. They pick up a single.
FOUR! FEROCIOUS! Just two men in the deep on the leg side and Shadab bowls a real bad ball. A long hop, landing in his half - Murray pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off, defended watchfully.
Shadab Khan now. 5-0-26-0 so far. Has struggled today.
Down the leg side, flicked away for a run.
The batsman does well to leave that bouncer.
FOUR! No feet movement, just hand-eye co-ordination. Full and wide outside off, Moor just stands there flat-footed and blasts it through the covers.
On middle and leg, defended from the crease.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
On middle and leg, flicked towards mid-wicket.
Hasan Ali is back on. 4-0-19-1 so far.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
FOUR! CREAMED! Murray getting his eye in now. A short ball outside off, Murray, unlike Moor, does not give it any respect. Pulls it with disdain over mid-wicket for a boundary!
Outside off, played through point for a single.
Another bouncer, same reaction from the batsman.
A bouncer now, asking the batsman to go after it but Moor ducks.
On a length outsider off, Murray waits for the ball to come to him and steers it to third man for a single.

Apparently, Pakistan are an over ahead in terms of the over rate. Have to confess - this is the first time I am seeing this type of a stat. Nice one though. We can see an early finish to the innings then.
The quicker one, on middle, pushed straight to short mid-wicket.
Floated outside off, eased towards long off for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On middle and leg, tucked behind square on the leg side for a run.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a single.
A lovely piece of bowling. Full and just outside off, watchfully defended back. Nothing much he could have done - the batsman, that is.
Outside off, punched off the back foot for a single.
Landed outside off, played straight to point.
Full and straight, pushed back to the bowler.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Faheem Ashraf is back on. He was initially brought on to bowl the 30th over but then probably, changed minds as this end might suit him better. 4-1-7-0 in his first spell.

SIX! Zimbabwe need more from Moor! Tossed up outside off, Moor decides to go downtown to break the shackles. Is successful as he lofts it with ease over the sightscreen! The stand is worth 10 from 14 balls.
A tad short, punched back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, eased through the covers for a run.
This one skids on with the angle, darts into the right-hander, Murray looks to drive it through the off side but gets it off the inner half towards mid-wicket.
Tries a similar shot but this time short mid-wicket dives to his left and parries it towards the bowler.
Full and around off, punched down the ground for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Short and outside off, punched through the off side for a run.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full and outside off, defended watchfully.
On middle and leg, flicked straight to mid-wicket.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Ryan Murray comes in.

OUT! That is a good catch and Pakistan have the breakthrough from the 7th bowler this morning. Tossed up outside off, Masakadza gets down and lines him up for another slog sweep. But he only manages to sky it up rather than getting the distance. Also, he chooses to hit it against the wind - not the best parameter to test your strength - only the heat of the sun can usually beat the force of the wind (had read it in a story when I was 8 years old). Seeing it demonstrated now. The fielder, Asif Ali comes running in from deep mid-wicket (after Sarfraz yells ASIF! ASIF! ASIFFFFFF!), loses the ball a bit in the air but manages to get to it and dives to take the catch. A fine 59 from the skipper - but could he have waited a bit more before playing the shot?
On middle and leg, pushed down to long on for a run. 'PAKDO KHUDI!' was the call. Too wide from the bowler.
Full and outside off, driven towards cover. 'PAKDO!' is the yell from Sarfraz. The fielder slides across to his right to stop.
On middle, a tad short, punched down to long on for a single.
Shoaib Malik time now. Surprising that it has taken Sarfraz so much time to bring the veteran on.
Full and outside off, driven crisply but straight to cover.
Short and outside off, punched back to the bowler.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Comes down the track, is not to the pitch of the ball, looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads.
SIX! That is a massive hit. Floated around off, Masakadza gets down and sweeps it wayyyy over square leg! 100 UP FOR ZIMBABWE! The run rate is on the up as well. The stand is worth 22 from 39 balls.
A short ball outside off, Masakadza looks to punch but the ball goes off the inner half of the bat back to the bowler.

London looking, turning Tokyo. Hmmm... best way to describe that shot. A short ball outside off, Masakadza looks to pull but is way too early into the stroke. The ball hits the back portion of the bat and lobs over cover! A single taken.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Slower through the air on the stump, Hamilton just checks his shot as he chips it back in the bowler's direction. Falls well short of him though.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Rocks onto the back foot and punches it to long off. Single to the total.
Positions himself well behind the line and defends.
Fifty for Hamilton Masakadza. 34th in ODIs. Has been a superb knock today. Needless to say, he has to carry on and score big. He eases this to long on and crosses over.
Slower through the air from around the wicket, a push-punch towards covers for nothing.
Interesting change. Fakhar Zaman into the attack. Let's see what he can produce.
Good timing on that from Moor. Cracks it through point for a brace.
Chooses to leave the ball outside the off stump.

Really nice shot from Hamilton Masakadza. Good balance as he stands tall to this back of a length ball and powerfully punches it through covers. Fakhar Zaman out in the deep moves to his right and cuts it off. The batsmen take three.
Places this shortish ball behind point and takes one.
Hurled outside off, Moor loosely plays at it and almost edges it. Bit of a risky shot, that.
Banged in short, tight line as it's close to off. Moor opens the face and dabs it down in front of point.
Short and flat outside off, punched away off the back foot on the off side.
Pushed away to the cover fielder. No run taken.
Short and turning in around off, Moor goes back and punches it to long on for a single.
PJ Moor has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Driven towards cover. No run taken yet again.
Low dipping full toss, worked straight to short mid-wicket.
Change of ends for Shadab Khan.
Peter Moor is off the mark. Slashes this wide ball outside off down towards third man. Runs the first one hard and completes the run.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Amir throws this in the off stump channel, it's away enough for the batsman to not do anything about it.
Moving away from around off, played to point. Dot ball.
Short of a length into the body, Hamilton whips it behind square leg and gets to the other end.
Good length delivery quite close to off, pushed down towards mid off for nothing.
Mohammad Amir returns to the attack.
Skidding off the surface, a googly, Moor does well to bring his bat down in time and keep it out.
Pats it past point and takes a comfortable single.
Dropped short and wide outside off, Hamilton cracks it square on the off side. In the gap and he comes back for the second.
A lot of air on this again, attacking the stumps, Hamilton plays it back in the bowler's direction.
Slower through the air as it's landed outside off, pushed away towards covers.
Floated on middle and off, Hamilton comes forward and blocks.
Good length ball on the stumps, kept out watchfully.
Peter Moor to bat next.

OUT! Hasan Ali strikes! A timely wicket for the Pakistan camp. This partnership was building steadily, they needed to break it and the pacer has done what he usually does. Keeps it fuller and straighter, brings it back in and catches Musakanda on the pads who looks to play across the line. Big shout and the umpire doesn't waste any time raising his finger. Maybe it was going down leg, but it doesn't matter to Pakistan.
It's been driven superbly through the covers. They pick up a single.
Outside off on a good length, opens the face of the bat and dabs it to point.
Keeps it out on the off side from the back foot again.
Back of a length around off, punched nicely through the covers for a run.
Pulls this short ball through mid-wicket for a couple more.
Lands it short again, cracked through covers for a single.
Flat and short outside off, cut through point and the batsmen will come back for two.
Loopy and full in line of the stumps, driven back to the bowler.
Short and wide outside off, punched through to sweeper cover for a single.

SIX! 10 off 2 balls for Hamilton against Shadab. He hit a boundary on the last ball of his previous over, now a biggie. High full toss from the leggie, possibly he's finding it difficult to grip the ball because of the cold. The Zimbabwe skipper accepts the gift on offer and mauls it over deep mid-wicket for a maximum. The 50-run stand is up with that as well.
Back of a length on off, played back to the bowler from within the crease.
Short again, pulled away again. Another single results as it placed to deep mid-wicket.
Muskanda with a good pull. Gets into position quickly, rises on his toes and hits it to deep mid-wicket as he changes ends.
Back of a length outside off, cut away square through point for one.
Attacks the off stump, Hamilton with a good head position defends it right under his nose.
Length delivery outside off, dabbed behind point for an easy single.
FOUR! Tremendous shot. Shadab drops it a bit short and Masakadza pulls it with disdain over mid-wicket. One bounce and into the ropes.
A short ball, pulled towards mid-wicket for a single.
That was a googly, outside off, Hamilton looked to punch but got a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
Comes down the track, takes it on the full and bunts it towards long on for a single.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Drinks break!
FOUR! Good way to end the over. Hamilton sees the room given outside off. It's short so he latches on to it with a fierce cut. Finds the point fence with no trouble. Superb shot.
Driven comfortably off the front foot through covers. One run to the total.

FOUR BYES! Not sure why a wide is not signalled, because that really flew. Hasan Ali with a bumper, Hamilton arches back and lets it be. Sarfraz leaps up to take it but even he can't reach it. Boundary results.
Short ball which is pulled to deep square leg for one run.
Attempts to run it down again, but can't beat short third man on this occasion.
Short and rising outside off, guided down to third man with an angled bat. Single collected.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Looped up googly on leg, Hamilton looks to play the sweep but loses his footing while doing so. Takes it on the pads and slips to the ground.
A firm punch from Hamilton, down to long on for one.
Works it with the wrists wide of the man at mid-wicket.
Another one flighted and pitched full, it's driven down the ground again, this time towards long on for a run.
Tossed up leg break on off, eased down to long off for a single.
Shadab Khan is on to roll his arm over.
Short and outside off, big cut shot from Masakadza, but the bounce gets too big on him to connect.
FOUR! Hammered! Hamilton taking the attack to the Pakistan bowlers. Fuller around off, the Zimbabwe captain smashes it past mid off to find the fence. Lovely sight to behold.
Opens the face slightly, dabs it away to point. Straight to the fielder so no run taken.
Keeps it tight, cramps Tarisai for room. He can only work it down in front of mid-wicket and scamper through for the single.
Angles it back in, it's flicked away through to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Some nice shape away from the right-hander. Hasan Ali bowls it in the off stump channel with some movement, Hamilton leaves it alone.
Hasan Ali is brought into the bowling attack.
Good effort from the fielder there. Full and outside off, driven crisply towards the covers. Imam there dives to his left and stops a certain boundary. Well done.
Hamilton gives the charge, so Faheem bowls it short. Forces the batsman to just block it.
Good length delivery on off stump, blocked in front of the cover fielder.
Tries punching it away through the covers, but mistimes it back down the track.
A bit fuller on the stumps, Hamilton rises and offers a firm punch down towards mid on.
Quick single. Sarfraz isn't happy with Amir at mid off, wants him to put more effort. Musakanda drives and both batsmen take off. Complete the run with ease too. Good running.
On the hips, glanced down towards fine leg for an easy run.
Back of a length outside off, Musakanda plays away from his body but gets beaten.

A misfield from Imam-ul-Haq. Sarfraz is not going to like that. Full around off, driven to extra cover where Imam lets it right through his palms. Probably because of the cold. It goes towards mid off and the batsmen take one.
Behind a length on off, Hamilton sticks his bat out to defend but gets an inside edge past the leg stump.

FOUR! That's dispatched from his sight! Good shot. Hamilton sees the ball landing short and instantly rocks onto his back foot. Pulls it with power through the mid-wicket region, leaving no fielder with any chance.
Angling in on middle and leg, driven just wide of mid on for a brisk run.
Moves inside the line and works it away towards mid-wicket. Dot ball to end the over.
Leans ahead to this fuller length ball and mistimes the drive towards mid on.
Camps on his back foot and defends it out.
Hasan Ali is seen warming up. Going to come on soon...
Back of a length outside off, punched off the back foot in front of cover.
Further away outside off, Hamilton shoulders his arms to it.
Good length delivery on the fourth stump line, left alone for the keeper to collect.
Powerplay 2 has been signalled. A maximum of 4 fielders will be allowed outside the 30-yard circle.
Fuller in length and on the stumps, kept out with the full face of the bat.
Short and into the body, defended down just wide of mid on for a quick single.
Goes full this time, on middle and off, another defensive shot on display.
Brings it in closer, on middle and off, blocked down with soft hands on the leg side.

Was there an edge? Faint appeal from the bowler, but nobody else has appealed. It's on a back of a length and it really kicks off the deck. Musakanda reaches out unnecessarily and tries to play at it, but the ball goes past the edge and into the keeper's gloves.
Shortish delivery outside off, Hamilton opens the bat face and with an angled bat, runs it down to third man. Jogs to the other end to complete the single.
Tarisai has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

FOUR! Shot. That's come from a man with confidence. Too full on off, Musakanda has no qualms in bashing this down the ground. Past the umpire and away to the boundary line in a jiffy. Made sweet connection on that.
Works this away to the point region, but won't get any run for it.
Back of a length, another block.

Play and a miss! Ashraf hurls it in the channel outside off, Musakanda frees his arms as he's given the chance to, but doesn't connect. Needs to be a little cautious, he wouldn't want to edge it behind like his teammates.
Length delivery coming back in, from around off, Musakanda leans across to get behind the line and then defends.
Well outside off, left alone to end the over.
Stays on the back foot and defends with a straight bat.
Usman hits the deck hard and pounds it in around off, Hamilton decides early he doesn't want to fiddle with that. Good decision, I'd say.
Moving away once again, Musakanda opens the face of the bat and runs it down to third man for a single. Off the mark with that.
On a good length on off, it is blocked.
Tarisai Musakanda to be the new man in.

OUT! Second wicket down! Needless from Chibhabha, was too far away to even play at it. At least for now. Usman hurls it well outside off, Chamu throws his bat at it, looking to fiercely cut it through point. All he can do though, is manage a healthy edge behind where Sarfraz dives low to his right and takes it safely in his gloves.

Short of a length outside off, Chibhabha punches it through covers. Asif Ali chases after it, after misfielding at first. Slides and throws it back in to Sarfraz. But, the captain is furious with Asif for the misfield. Gives him a long, hard stare. Cold morning in Bulawayo, but Sarfraz is the only one who doesn't need a jacket probably.
This back of a length delivery is kept out safely by Chamu.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Stays right behind the line and meets it with a straight blade in defense.
Outside off on a good length, Chamu fails to make any kind of connection with his bat.
Marginally ahead of a length, on the off stick, Chamu Chibhabha with a front foot defensive shot.
Faheem Ashraf into the attack.
FOUR! Lovely shot. Full and right in the slot for Hamilton, he clears his front leg and whip-drives it through the right of mid on for a boundary.
Sharp movement away and looking at this, the Zimbabwe captain doesn't bother himself with it.
Plants his front foot forward and drives the full ball straight to mid off.
Back of a length outside off, Hamilton hangs his bat inside the line but then withdraws his bat at the last second.
Short of a length, moving away from off, the batsman leans across a bit and defends it out.
Slants it across on a fullish length, punched between point and cover-point for a single.
Aiming the top of off stump, blocked solidly back down the track by getting behind the line. 9 off the over.
Shooting off the surface after it lands on a length, Hamilton leaves it alone.
FOUR! Again, just a little bit of width offered and Hamilton this time has pounced on it. Full and wide outside off, driven hard a bit square through cover-point for a boundary.
Full ball on the stumps, driven to mid off. Chari instantly goes for the run, takes the fielder on and gets to the other end in good time. Nicely done.
Turns it away on the leg side but won't get any run for it.

FOUR! First of the innings for Zimbabwe! Shortish and wide enough outside off, Chari has a chances to free his arms which he does. Flashes it through point and the ball races away to the boundary line in no time.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump. A wicket-maiden from Usman Khan, lovely stuff from him.
Back of a length, Usman keeping the line really tight, Hamilton blocks again.
Further outside off, Hamilton has nothing to do with that.
Hamilton Masakadza walks in at no.3.

OUT! Gone! The first duck's dead. Pakistan get their early breakthrough. He kept bringing it back in till now, then suddenly sends it the other way and gets the desired result. Usman Khan slants across a length delivery around off, Chari looks to punch this away from his body through the covers but only manages an edge behind. Skipper Sarfraz takes a regulation catch and completes the formalities.
On a length once again, Chari is rock solid in defense.
Length ball on middle and off, Chari guards it out safely.

Another loud shout for a leg before, not given once more. Pitching outside leg it seems. Full around the pads, Chibhabha misses the flick and is caught low on the pads. Amir turns and pleads to the umpire, but it's the right call. Well done.
Hangs back inside the crease and offers another defensive stroke in response on the off side.
Keeps it close to off, a length ball. Chibhabha opens the bat face and taps it away to the man at point.
Wide! Banged in short but it's too short, wide signalled by the umpire.
Back of a length, outside off, not much movement on this occasion, tapped down on the off side.
Fuller length delivery on middle and off, Chibhabha drives this off the inner half in front of square leg for nothing.
Amir serves it on off. It's a length ball which nips in slightly and skids a touch as well. Chamu Chibhabha just about manages to keep it out.
Works it away from within the crease with a closed faced towards square leg. Another tight over comes to an end.
Just behind a length, on off, another rap on the thigh pad as Chari fails to connect. That one skidded off the surface a bit too, probably that's the reason why.
Angles it across, just outside off, Chari stands tall and tamely punches it in front of covers.
Length ball on middle and off, slanting away slightly, punched defensively back down the track.
Short of a good length on middle and leg, a swipe across the line from Brian but he fails to connect. Takes a blow around the hips.
Wide! Hmmm... Seemed like there was some noise as the ball passed the bat. Way down the leg side, Chari looks to pull it fine down the leg side but misses.
Full and attacking the stumps immediately, Chari comes half-forward, attempts to drive it back down the ground but gets an inside edge onto his pads instead.
Usman Khan to bowl from the other end with the second new ball.

First runs of the morning and the innings for Zimbabwe. Length delivery further outside off, Chari reaches out to it and gets it off the outer half down to third man for a single. Good first over from Amir, just the 1 run from it.
Shaping away from around off, no-brainer for Chari to let it be.

Big shout for lbw, turned down. Height clearly an issue. Little bit of movement back into the right-hander from Amir. On a length, some extra bounce as Chari is forward to defend. Gets rapped on the back thigh pad, no response from the umpire.
Better line. Outside off on a good length, arms are shouldered to this one.
Good length delivery, once again a fraction too straight in line, Chari works it down in front of mid-wicket.
Lands it on a good length on middle and leg, kicks off the deck a bit as Chari looks to defend. Wears it on the thigh pads instead as he misses his block.

We are ready to begin. Chamu Chibhabha and Brian Chari will open the innings for the hosts, while Mohammad Amir will take the first new ball for Pakistan on this chilly Bulawayo morning. It's freezing out there, going to be a tough stay for the fielders in the middle. Two slips in place. Here we go...
TOSS - Zimbabwe win the toss and opt to bat first! There are no changes in the playing XI, both sides are going in with the same team.

Hello and welcome for the 2nd of this 5-match series between Zimbabwe and Pakistan. The first game saw a strong collective showing from the Men in Green, beating Zimbabwe in all departments. The hosts had key players missing as it is, but injuries to more, in particular Solomon Mire, who's been their best batsmen, is a big blow. And to add to that, Malcolm Waller pulling out of the series is not a good sign either. So, an already depleted side, coming on the back of a defeat, have an uphill task against them. They have some fresh faces in the side, so a positive is that they can gain some valuable experience. Pakistan more or less have all their boxes ticked, so they'll be hoping to put in another solid showing. Let's see how it all unfolds...
